message.content:
I'm planning a new feature for KasirKu (G:\PROJECT1\KasirKu, Next.js + Supabase multi-tenant POS/finance SaaS). We're adding a new billing plan tier called "Finance Only" — customers who already have their own POS/cashier system, who want to buy just the Akuntansi/SDM (accounting/HR) module without paying for or seeing the Kasir/POS features.

I need a precise understanding of the current billing + navigation gating architecture so I can plan where to hook in a new plan type. Please investigate and report back with file paths + line numbers + code snippets where relevant:

1. **Billing plans**: Read `src/lib/billing/plans.ts` fully. How is `PlanCode` used downstream — grep for `PlanCode`, `getPlan(`, `plan_code` across the codebase. Where is a business's active plan/subscription stored (which table, which column) and how is "is this business allowed to use feature X" currently checked anywhere (any existing per-feature gating, even for business_type)?

2. **Business type gating**: Read `src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/dashboard-shell.tsx` fully, especially the `buildNavGroups` function and how `business_type` (`fnb`/`retail`/`tiket`) currently filters which nav items/groups show. I want to understand the exact pattern used so a new "finance-only plan" gate can follow the same style (or explain if it should be a different mechanism, e.g. a boolean/plan-code check instead of the business_type union).

3. **Billing gate / paywall pattern**: Find where the app currently blocks access when a subscription is expired/past-due (search for "past due", "expired", billing banner, redirect-to-billing logic — likely near `src/lib/billing/` and possibly inside `dashboard-shell.tsx` or a layout file). I want to see the existing gate mechanism (redirect? banner? disabled buttons?) since "hide POS nav for finance-only plan" will probably reuse a similar check pattern.

4. **Business creation / signup flow**: Where does a new business get created and its `business_type` set (search for "business_type" insert, onboarding/signup page)? Is `business_type` ever changed after creation, or picked once at signup? I want to know if a similar "plan_code chosen at signup" flow exists to model after.

5. Briefly note the schema of the `businesses` table and the `payments`/subscriptions table (whichever table stores active plan) — column names only, no need for full DDL, just enough to know what a query/check would look like.

Report factually with file:line references. No need to propose a solution — I'll design that myself from your findings.

I now have a complete picture of the billing and navigation-gating architecture. Here's the report.

## 1. Billing plans (`src/lib/billing/plans.ts`)

Full file (22 lines):
```ts
export type PlanCode = "monthly" | "yearly" | "lifetime";

export type Plan = {
  code: PlanCode;
  name: string;
  kind: "subscription" | "lifetime";
  periodDays: number | null; // null = lifetime, never expires
  price: number;
};

export const PLANS: Plan[] = [
  { code: "monthly", name: "Langganan Bulanan", kind: "subscription", periodDays: 30, price: 99000 },
  { code: "yearly", name: "Langganan Tahunan", kind: "subscription", periodDays: 365, price: 990000 },
  { code: "lifetime", name: "Sekali Bayar (Lifetime)", kind: "lifetime", periodDays: null, price: 2500000 },
];

export function getPlan(code: string): Plan | undefined {
  return PLANS.find((p) => p.code === code);
}
```
Note: `PlanCode` is defined but `getPlan(code: string)` takes a loose `string`, not `PlanCode` — nothing actually enforces the union at the DB/query boundary. `plan_code` is stored as plain `text` in Postgres (no CHECK constraint tying it to `PLANS`), so today plans are purely a **pricing/display** concept, not a **feature-entitlement** concept.

**Where `PlanCode`/`getPlan`/`plan_code` are used:**
- `src/lib/billing/plans.ts:3,19` — definition.
- `src/app/business/[businessId]/billing/actions.ts:5,17,43` — `createPayment()`: looks up plan by code, inserts a `payments` row with `plan_code`.
- `src/app/business/[businessId]/billing/page.tsx:4,48,92` — renders `PLANS.map(...)` as pricing cards; looks up `currentPlan` via `getPlan(access.planCode)` purely for display.
- `src/app/admin/actions.ts:5,22,29-35` — `activateSubscriptionManually()`: admin manually activates a subscription by plan code, calls RPC `admin_activate_subscription`.
- `src/app/api/midtrans/notification/route.ts:4,124-154` — webhook: on settled payment, looks up the plan and **writes** `subscriptions.plan_code`/`status`/`period_end`.
- `src/app/onboarding/actions.ts:49` — inserts initial `subscriptions` row with `plan_code: ""`, `status: "unpaid"` (no plan chosen yet).

**Nowhere is `plan_code` read to gate a *feature* (module) — only to gate overall dashboard access (locked/unlocked) and to display pricing/labels.** There is no existing per-feature plan check anywhere in the codebase (searched `PlanCode`, `getPlan(`, `plan_code` exhaustively — 5-6 files total, all listed above).

**Active plan/subscription storage:**
- Table `public.subscriptions` (defined `supabase/migrations/20260712110000_billing.sql:15-23`): one row per business (`business_id uuid unique`), columns `plan_code text`, `status text check in ('unpaid','active','past_due','expired')`, `period_end timestamptz` (null = lifetime), `updated_at`.
- Read via `getSubscriptionAccess()` in `src/lib/billing/status.ts:15-36`.

## 2. Business-type gating (`dashboard-shell.tsx`)

Full file: `src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/dashboard-shell.tsx`.

- `BusinessType = "fnb" | "retail" | "tiket"` (line 50) — a closed string union, passed as a **prop** down from the server layout (not fetched client-side).
- `buildNavGroups(businessId, businessType)` (lines 52-152) is a **pure function** that returns an array of `NavGroup = { title, items: NavItem[] }`. It's called once per render in `SidebarContent` (line 187), so gating happens by literally omitting array entries at nav-group construction time — not by hiding/disabling rendered items.
- Gating style is inline ternary/spread inside the array literals:
  - `isFnb`/`isTiket` booleans derived once at top of function (lines 53-54).
  - Whole items conditionally spread in: `...(isTiket ? [] : [ ...5 finance items... ])` (lines 61-70) — hides cash-basis "Keuangan" reports for `tiket`.
  - Whole `items` array swapped per type in the "Operasional" group: `items: isTiket ? [...ticket ops...] : [...retail/fnb ops...]` (lines 109-133), with a nested `...(isFnb ? [...] : [])` for F&B-only items (117-127).
  - **"Akuntansi" and "SDM" groups are never filtered by business_type** — every business type currently sees the full Akuntansi/SDM nav (lines 80-106, 135-143). This is the natural seam: a "Finance Only" plan would need to gate at the **group level** (hide "Operasional" group's non-accounting items, hide the standalone "Buka Kasir" button) rather than reusing the existing per-item business_type conditionals, since those only ever *rearrange* POS-ish items across business types, never hide the POS concept entirely.
- Outside `buildNavGroups`, `businessType` is also used for the subtitle label (`BUSINESS_TYPE_SUBTITLE`, lines 154-158) and is a required prop threaded through `SidebarContent`/`DashboardShell` (lines 172-186, 314-328).
- Separate from the sidebar nav, there's a hardcoded **"Buka Kasir" button** at lines 213-222 (always rendered, links to `/business/${businessId}/pos`) that is not part of `buildNavGroups` at all — it would need its own conditional for a finance-only plan.
- `businessType` comes from `src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/layout.tsx:17,34` — a server-side query `supabase.from("businesses").select("id, name, business_type")`, cast `as "fnb" | "retail" | "tiket"`, passed to `<DashboardShell businessType={...}>`. Since it's a prop (not client-fetched), a `plan_code`/entitlement gate could be added at exactly this point (fetch alongside `business` and `access` in the `Promise.all`, lines 16-20) and threaded the same way.

## 3. Billing gate / paywall pattern

- `src/lib/billing/status.ts:15-36` — `getSubscriptionAccess(supabase, businessId)` queries `subscriptions` (`plan_code, status, period_end`) for the business and returns `{ locked, status, planCode, periodEnd }`. `locked = status === "unpaid" || status === "expired"`. `active` and `past_due` are both *not* locked — `past_due` only degrades to a warning banner (comment at lines 12-14 explicitly documents the grace-period design).
- Enforcement point: `src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/layout.tsx:19,26-28` — server layout calls `getSubscriptionAccess`, and if `access.locked`, does a hard `redirect(`/business/${businessId}/billing`)` before rendering `DashboardShell`/children at all. This is a **full redirect gate**, not a partial/disabled-UI gate, and it wraps the entire `(dashboard)` route group (so it also covers Akuntansi/SDM pages, but notably **not** `/business/[businessId]/pos`, which lives outside the `(dashboard)` group and has its own `page.tsx` with no subscription check — see `src/app/business/[businessId]/pos/page.tsx`, which only checks `business` existence and cashier PIN session, no `getSubscriptionAccess` call).
- Soft/non-blocking case (`past_due`): surfaced as an amber banner inside `DashboardShell` itself, not the layout — `dashboard-shell.tsx:380-398`, driven by the `billingPastDuePeriodEnd` prop computed in `layout.tsx:36` (`access.status === "past_due" ? access.periodEnd : null`). Banner shows the overdue date and a "Bayar Sekarang" link to `/business/${businessId}/billing`; it doesn't block interaction with the rest of the page.
- The billing page itself (`src/app/business/[businessId]/billing/page.tsx`) is the un-gated landing spot — reachable regardless of lock state, renders current status badge (`STATUS_LABELS`/`STATUS_BADGE`, lines 12-24) and the plan picker (`PLANS.map`, line 92), currently manual/WhatsApp-driven per `BILLING_MANUAL_MODE` (`src/lib/billing/config.ts:7`) rather than the live Midtrans `PayButton`.
- No per-feature/per-module gate exists anywhere today (confirmed by the `PlanCode`/`plan_code` grep in section 1) — the only existing gate is the binary all-or-nothing dashboard lock in `layout.tsx`. A "finance-only plan hides POS nav" feature would be a **new** mechanism, structurally most similar to the `businessType` prop-threading pattern in section 2 (fetch once in `layout.tsx`, pass down as a prop to `DashboardShell`/`buildNavGroups`) rather than an extension of `getSubscriptionAccess`'s locked/unlocked boolean.

## 4. Business creation / signup flow

- Onboarding UI: `src/app/onboarding/onboarding-form.tsx` — radio buttons for `business_type` (`fnb`/`retail`/`tiket`), lines 60-107, required field, no plan/pricing selection happens here at all.
- Server action: `src/app/onboarding/actions.ts:8-58` (`createBusiness`):
  - Validates `businessType` is one of the 3 literals (lines 27-29).
  - Inserts into `businesses` with `owner_id`, `name`, `business_type` (lines 31-38).
  - Immediately inserts a companion `subscriptions` row with `plan_code: ""`, `status: "unpaid"` (lines 47-51) — comment at 45-46 explains: no trial, owner must pick & pay before entering dashboard/POS.
  - Redirects straight to `/business/${business.id}/billing` (line 57) — so plan selection happens **after** business creation, on the billing page, not during onboarding. `business_type` is chosen once at signup; `plan_code` is chosen afterward on a separate page/flow. There is no unified "choose type + plan together" step today.
- `business_type` **can** be changed later, but only pre-first-transaction: `src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/settings/actions.ts:288-321` (function starting ~line 288) — checks `transactions`/`ticket_transactions` are empty (lines 301-312), then does `supabase.from("businesses").update({ business_type: businessType }).eq("id", businessId)` (lines 314-317), else returns a Indonesian error message that the type is locked once transactions exist. **`plan_code`, by contrast, is never directly settings-editable by the owner** — it only changes via the Midtrans webhook (`api/midtrans/notification/route.ts:146-154`) or the admin RPC `admin_activate_subscription` (`src/app/admin/actions.ts:29-35`, migration `supabase/migrations/20260712130000_admin_activate_subscription.sql`). So there is no "plan_code chosen at signup and locked" flow to model after — plan changes are exclusively a payment/admin-driven mutation on the existing subscription row, never a form field the owner edits directly.

## 5. Schema summary

**`public.businesses`** (`supabase/migrations/20260702100100_businesses_and_cashiers.sql:3-20`, constraint widened in `20260706200000_ticket_venue.sql:8-12`):
`id, owner_id, name, business_type (text, check in fnb/retail/tiket), address, phone, npwp, logo_url, tax_enabled, tax_rate, service_enabled, service_rate, auto_lock_enabled, auto_lock_minutes, recovery_code_hash, created_at`

**`public.subscriptions`** (`supabase/migrations/20260712110000_billing.sql:15-23`):
`id, business_id (uuid, unique fk → businesses), plan_code (text), status (text, check in unpaid/active/past_due/expired), period_end (timestamptz, null=lifetime), updated_at`

**`public.payments`** (append-only Midtrans audit log, `20260712110000_billing.sql:39-51`):
`id, business_id (fk), plan_code, order_id (unique), amount, status (check in pending/settlement/expire/cancel/deny), midtrans_transaction_id, payment_type, raw_notification (jsonb), created_at`

RLS note (same migration, lines 8-14, 26-37, 55-63): writes from the authenticated client are narrow — a business can only insert its own initial `unpaid` subscription and `pending` payments; every real state transition (`plan_code`/`status`/`period_end` changes) is done exclusively by the service-role Midtrans webhook or admin RPC, never directly by the tenant. Any new `plan_code` values (e.g. a `"finance_only"` tier) would need to flow through these same service-role-only mutation paths.
